claim: Let \(n=(n_1,\ldots,n_S)\) be an unlabeled strictly positive integer abundance profile with total \(N\), and define individual-based rarefied expected richness for a uniform sample without replacement of size \(m\) by \(R_m(n)=\sum_{i=1}^{S}\left[1-\binom{N-n_i}{m}/\binom{N}{m}\right]\). Compare two profiles only when they have the same total \(N\) and the same species richness \(S\). No two such profiles reverse their strict ordering under \(R_m\) at two interior sample sizes when \(N\le9\). At \(N=10\), exactly one unordered pair up to species permutation has a strict rarefaction crossing: \(A=(6,2,2)\) and \(B=(5,4,1)\), necessarily with \(S=3\). The profile \(B\) has greater expected rarefied richness at \(m=2\) and \(m=3\), while \(A\) has greater expected rarefied richness for every \(m=4,\ldots,9\); the curves agree at \(m=1\) and \(m=10\). Explicitly, \(R_2(A)=73/45<74/45=R_2(B)\), \(R_3(A)=61/30<41/20=R_3(B)\), and \(R_4(A)=163/70>242/105=R_4(B)\). The mechanism joins two exact endpoint statistics: \(R_2=2-\sum_i n_i(n_i-1)/(N(N-1))\), whereas \(R_{N-1}=S-f_1/N\), where \(f_1\) is the number of singleton species. Thus \(B\) is favored at small samples because it has smaller finite-sample Simpson concentration, but \(A\) is favored near complete census because it has no singleton while \(B\) has one. Therefore ten individuals is the smallest fixed-richness census at which the choice of rarefaction sample size can reverse an expected-richness comparison, and the complete first crossing layer consists of this single pair.
integrity: The finite census is exhaustive through the claimed boundary. Two independent generators produce identical abundance-profile sets at every total and richness; every same-richness pair is compared at every interior sample size using exact rational arithmetic. The witness is additionally checked through closed endpoint identities linking sample size two to finite-sample Simpson concentration and sample size \(N-1\) to singleton count.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns strictly positive integer abundance profiles compared at common census size and common observed species richness under individual-based hypergeometric rarefaction. It is an exact statement about expected rarefied richness, not about sampling uncertainty, incidence-based rarefaction, coverage-based standardization, or extrapolation.
title: Ten individuals are the sharp fixed-richness rarefaction-crossing boundary
